_comment: klt erc supply spec for the digital partition's routed GDS -- the
structural power-delivery read T1 item 11 (klayout-tools#2025, tracked
here as issue #268) grades from. Run it with:
klt erc layout/digital/trng_top.gds layout/digital/erc-supply-spec.json \
--top trng_top --format json
What this spec asserts, and why each piece is shaped this way:
- `stackup[0]` MUST carry `role: "gate"` (klt erc's own contract), so the
stack starts at Poly2 rather than at Metal1. `active_layer` (Comp) makes
the antenna denominator `poly n diff` instead of raw poly area, which is
what keeps the filltie/endcap/filler cells' gate-less poly bars out of
`gates[]` entirely instead of reporting non-physical antenna ratios for
them (klayout-tools docs/cli/erc.md, 'Gate area').
- Metal1-Metal5 are the conductor order this block's own PDN and routing
use: place-and-route put the followpin straps on Metal1 (0.9 um width,
5.04 um pitch), the row-crossing straps on Metal4 (4.48 um / 44.8 um)
and the top grid on Metal5 (4.48 um / 89.6 um) -- every
`power.straps[].layer` of layout/digital/reports/place_and_route.json is
covered by this stackup, as item 11's digital claim requires. Metal2 and
Metal3 are signal routing; they stay in the stack because the
fabrication order must be contiguous for the via chain to bridge it, but
they carry no supply text of their own.
- `label_layer` only on the two layers this merged GDS actually puts
supply text on -- verified against the stream itself, not assumed:
34/10 carries the gf180mcu_fd_sc_mcu9t5v0 standard cells' own PG pin
text (94 `VDD` + 94 `VSS` labels), 81/10 carries the PDN's top-level
supply pin text (one `vddd` + one `vss`). Metal4's 46/10 text is
signal-pin-only, so declaring it would add nothing.
- GDS layer numbers are gf180mcuD's own drawn-layer numbers (the variant
sim/pdk.json pins), derived from the PDK's own
libs.tech/klayout/tech/gf180mcu.lyp and cross-checked against
klayout-tools' curated gf180mcu deck layer table -- both agree on every
entry above.
- `nets[]`: one declared name per physical supply, both `kind: "supply"`,
which is what makes a short between them report as the severe
`erc.supply_short` rather than the general `erc.multiply_driven_net`.
The declared spellings are the 34/10 ones (`VDD`/`VSS`) because those
labels sit on every standard-cell row rail, so a rail-to-grid split
anywhere in the PDN resolves the name to more than one electrical
island and fires `erc.unconnected_net`. The same two islands also
carry the 81/10 spellings `vddd`/`vss` -- this block's authoritative
power_net/ground_net names -- via the top-level PDN pins; declaring
BOTH spellings would report that intentional same-net aliasing as a
false `erc.supply_short`, so the spec declares exactly one name per
supply. Each declared supply resolving to exactly ONE island (zero
`erc.unconnected_net` and zero `erc.supply_short` naming it) is the
pass condition -- a zero count is that verdict, not merely an absence.
- There is deliberately NO `ties[]` section here, and that is a recorded
gap rather than an oversight: klt erc's tie extraction collapses a real
routed standard-cell design into one electrical island and reports a
FALSE `erc.supply_short` -- filed upstream as klayout-tools#2169. So
`ties[]` is omitted, which per klt erc's own contract means
`erc.missing_tie` is NOT computed rather than reported as a misleading
zero (klayout-tools docs/cli/erc.md: 'Omitted entirely -> never
computed'); the `ties_disclosure` key below carries that statement into
the report itself. The standing-in well-tie evidence, named per #268:
place-and-route filled every row with
gf180mcu_fd_sc_mcu9t5v0__filltie tapcells (`power.tapcell_master`,
`power.pdn: true`, layout/digital/reports/place_and_route.json) plus
endcap/filler masters, its power-isolation check found exactly the two
expected supply nets (vddd/vss) and no entropy-supply shorting, and LVS
matches on the same build (layout/digital/reports/lvs.json, `status:
"match"`, `mismatch_count: 0`) -- a netlist-level statement that the
taps are present and connected, which is what stands in for the
uncomputed `erc.missing_tie`.

ties_disclosure.reason: The filltie tapcells are expressible geometry, but klt erc's tie extraction collapses this routed standard-cell design into one electrical island and reports a false erc.supply_short (klayout-tools#2169), so no ties[] is declared and erc.missing_tie is not computed. Standing-in well-tie evidence: power.tapcell_master gf180mcu_fd_sc_mcu9t5v0__filltie across every row with power.pdn true (layout/digital/reports/place_and_route.json), its power-isolation check ok on exactly vddd/vss, and LVS status match with mismatch_count 0 on the same build (layout/digital/reports/lvs.json).
